headline: NJ Deputy AG arrested for producing AI CSAM, say cops
summary: Brian Richard Fitzgerald, a New Jersey deputy attorney general, was charged with felony counts related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material after a Discord tip.
details: Brian Richard Fitzgerald, a New Jersey deputy attorney general, was arrested on felony charges related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM). This follows a tip received by the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children in July.

Fitzgerald is accused of using AI to transform social media photos of real minors into sexualized images, which he then distributed online. Authorities utilized digital forensics and subscriber records linked to a Discord account, "thegentlemanpervert_2160_07833," to trace the user to Fitzgerald's home address.

A search of his residence uncovered prompts and scripts used to create AI CSAM, along with Discord chat logs where Fitzgerald allegedly admitted to making and sharing multiple illicit images. The Department of Justice has previously clarified that AI-generated CSAM is legally considered CSAM.

Fitzgerald, who had served as deputy attorney general since 2016, faces charges including possession of CSAM, dissemination of CSAM, and criminal use of a communication facility. This case marks a rare instance where a high-ranking state law enforcement official is accused of such crimes.

New Jersey’s district attorney, Joe Khan, stated that no one is above the law and vowed aggressive prosecution. Similar arrests for AI-generated illicit content have also occurred with law enforcement officers in Pennsylvania and Korea.

headline_marked: [[Llama.cpp on jailbroken PS5]] now runs any GGUF model natively on the console
headline: Llama.cpp on jailbroken PS5 now runs any GGUF model natively on the console
summary: PS5LM transforms a jailbroken PS5 into a private, local AI model server, allowing it to run GGUF models on its GPU without needing a PC or cloud services.
details: A new project, PS5LM, enables jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles to run GGUF language models directly on their GPUs. This turns the console into a private model server, accessible by other devices on the network, such as laptops and phones.

The system operates independently, requiring no external PC, cloud services, or account. It also supports new decision models, compatible with the /v1/systemone API used by Ollaya, providing typed decisions with calibrated probabilities in a fraction of a second.

PS5LM is designed for PS5 consoles running firmware versions 7.00 to 13.60, provided they are jailbroken and have the necessary payloads loaded. It has been demonstrated running models like Qwen 3.5 9B and supports decision models such as d1 Omni 600M, d1 3B, and Clef Flash.

The project is built on C++ using ps5-homebrew-ui and integrates llama.cpp with ggml-vulkan on PS5_Vulkan's RADV. It is open-source under the GPL-3.0-or-later license, with llama.cpp retaining its MIT license, and is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment.
